content:
For any connected graph on 2019 vertices, take a spanning tree. A tree with \(n\) vertices can always be covered by at most \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\) simple paths, by induction:

- If a vertex has two leaf neighbors \(x,y\), delete \(x,y\), cover the remaining tree, and add the path \(x-v-y\).
- Otherwise, deleting all leaves leaves a smaller tree; a leaf \(y\) of it has exactly one leaf neighbor \(x\) in the original tree and degree \(2\). Delete \(x,y\), cover the rest, and add path \(x-y\).

Thus every connected graph on 2019 vertices can be covered by at most  
\[
\lfloor 2019/2\rfloor = 1009
\]
lines.

Now consider a star with one center and \(2018\) leaves. A single path in a star can contain at most two leaves, so covering all \(2018\) leaves requires at least  
\[
2018/2 = 1009
\]
lines. Hence some graph needs exactly \(1009\) lines, so orders with \(k\le 1008\) can be impracticable, while \(k=1009\) always works.

\[
\boxed{1008}
\]
